body: Haven't checked the specific details of this case but the description of this particular method is incorrect, it does not have to be inside the tree, it just have to have been marked as ready, so that at least needs to be corrected in the documentation

Also haven't checked this particular case but it doesn't have anything to do specifically with the Curve. A simple example showcasing the behavior:
```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	var n := Node.new()
	prints(n.is_inside_tree(), n.is_node_ready()) # false false

	add_child(n) # Marks `n` as ready.
	prints(n.is_inside_tree(), n.is_node_ready()) # true true

	remove_child(n)
	prints(n.is_inside_tree(), n.is_node_ready()) # false true

	n.request_ready() # Resets `n` to be again marked as not ready.
	prints(n.is_inside_tree(), n.is_node_ready()) # false false
	
	n.queue_free()
```
The docs are inprecise.

For reference it just maps to the internal `ready_first` flag:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/64596092ae60e8fc10da7b61ac024d099a80a3b7/scene/main/node.h#L287
Initialization:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/64596092ae60e8fc10da7b61ac024d099a80a3b7/scene/main/node.cpp#L4116
Check/resetting:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/64596092ae60e8fc10da7b61ac024d099a80a3b7/scene/main/node.cpp#L3556-L3563
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/64596092ae60e8fc10da7b61ac024d099a80a3b7/scene/main/node.cpp#L3867-L3868
Trigerring notification (which leads to calling script `_ready` override) and signal after entering the SceneTree:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/64596092ae60e8fc10da7b61ac024d099a80a3b7/scene/main/node.cpp#L336-L340

Checking further the code in question doesn't do anything outside the editor, in that case I'd expect the node to be moved around occasionally and trigger the state where it is ready but not in the tree due to how the editor handles that

So the documentation should be made clearer, but for the editor I don't think users can expect the nodes in the tree to behave "normally" and not be detached and reattached to the tree as the editor does its thing

> Also haven't checked this particular case but it doesn't have anything to do specifically with the Curve. 

Yes and no. This signal connection pattern is one I use in all my editor tooling. No other resource fires the `changed` signal during scene reload. In my tools, I use `is_node_ready` as a safety check so it doesn't just do a bunch of operations when exported properties are set on scene load. This present issue causes this check to fail, and creates a bug if my operation depends on the node to be ready, such as getting a path or using get_tree or global_transform.

So yes, the documentation can be clarified for is_node_ready. But I would say that Curve should still not be firing the changed signal unexpectedly.

I don't know that there's any expectation that's violated here, I don't know that the expectation of that in tool is a reasonable expectation, as with the above, so relying on that assumption isn't safe so the proper checks should be in place if you rely on that assumption

Nothing else behaving in a particular way is not reason alone, so it'd be something that's an established expectation of how the engine works, documented for example
But regardless I'd say that's something to track in a separate issue report so this can focus on the documentation, as it's two unrelated conversations

> So the documentation should be made clearer, but for the editor I don't think users can expect the nodes in the tree to behave "normally" and not be detached and reattached to the tree as the editor does its thing

Agreed that editor should be able to do weird things to nodes in the editor. The issue is that tool scripts shouldn't be unexpectedly roped into receiving signals from places they didn't intend to. Connecting to `changed` is very intentional, and this issue breaks that intent.

> I don't know that there's any expectation that's violated here, I don't know that the expectation of that in tool is a reasonable expectation, as with the above, so relying on that assumption isn't safe so the proper checks should be in place if you rely on that assumption

It isn't reasonable to ask tool devs to put in every possible check before every single action. By that logic I should be putting in a null check, queued_for_deletion check, ready check, scene tree check, editor hint check, every single time I want to respond to "the user wiggled a curve".

Put simply, the expectation that's being broken is that the Curve is firing a changed signal when it hasn't been changed. This is an outlier that breaks an otherwise well-used pattern.

I don't see that that assumption is broken here though, you are in the editor, the editor operates on data in the editor, so this doesn't seem to be an issue with how `Curve` sends signals, at most it would be an issue with how the editor inspector for example operates on curves (and we'd need to evaluate if this is exclusive to `Curve` or not)

But I'd say that it's reasonable to expect that the editor makes changes to resources open in the editor as part of the interface, rollback and rollforward in various ways, but we'd need to evaluate this in general and in particular, it could be specific to the curve editor having some bug

But I'd say to open a new issue to track that part, as this should focus on the documentation details for `is_node_ready`, which is unrelated to this conversation

Edit: To clarify:
* This issue report specifically should be about the description of `is_node_ready`, and is unrelated to `Curve` or the editor behavior
* The issue is not about `Curve` emitting `changed`, it's about the editor making changes to `Curve` through the editor systems in unexpected ways, and that should be discussed, but in a separate issue, and should be clear about what is the issue, i.e. it's *technically* unrelated to `Curve`, it's about how the editor does modifications in the open scene

>     * The issue is not about `Curve` emitting `changed`, it's about the editor making changes to `Curve` through the editor systems in unexpected ways, and that should be discussed, but in a separate issue, and should be clear about what is the issue, i.e. it's _technically_ unrelated to `Curve`, it's about how the editor does modifications in the open scene

I've changed the present issue description to be just about the documentation, and created a separate issue about the signal here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/117802

But counterpoint: that new issue _should_ be treated specific to `Curve` until a more general pattern is established. This does not just happen with every exported resource, and there is abundant precedent of specific classes emitting signals redundantly or inappropriately in the editor. i.e., even if the _conditions_ under which the signal emission are routine for an editor context (e.g. nodes being moved around by the editor), it doesn't mean the signal emission is an appropriate response.
